definitions.gloss: Roman letters, romaji, the Latin alphabet
definitions.explanation: The Latin alphabet (A-Z) used to write Japanese phonetically. Also refers to the romanization system itself.

examples.japanese: ⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ローマ{字|じ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: Write your name in Roman letters.

examples.japanese: ⟦パスポート→パスポート：00341_pasupooto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ローマ{字|じ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{氏名|しめい}→氏名：04033_shimei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{記載|きさい}→記載：14169_kisai⟧⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Names are written in Roman letters on passports.

examples.japanese: ローマ{字|じ}⟦{入力|にゅうりょく}→入力：04769_nyuuryoku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧な⟦{入力|にゅうりょく}→入力：04769_nyuuryoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦どちら→どちら：00927_dochira⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}っています→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Do you use romaji input or kana input?

notes:
ローマ{字|じ} literally means "Roman characters" and refers to the Latin alphabet as used to represent Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ローマ{字|じ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧: to write in romaji
- ローマ{字|じ}⟦{入力|にゅうりょく}→入力：04769_nyuuryoku⟧: romaji input (typing method)
- ローマ{字|じ}⟦{表記|ひょうき}→表記：14123_hyouki⟧: romaji notation

ROMANIZATION SYSTEMS:
There are several romanization systems, including {訓令式|くんれいしき} (Kunrei-shiki, taught in Japanese schools) and ヘボン{式|しき} (Hepburn, used on passports and signs). Hepburn is the most widely recognized internationally.

USAGE:
Most Japanese people type using ローマ{字|じ}⟦{入力|にゅうりょく}→入力：04769_nyuuryoku⟧, where they type romanized letters that are automatically converted to kana.
